jobs.title: Data Center OFE - Sourcing Lead, Data Center Power & Cooling
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic is building AI compute at a scale and pace that outruns what off-the-shelf data center equipment was designed for. Much of the power and cooling equipment behind our next campuses — battery energy storage systems (BESS), grid-forming and grid-following inverters, solid-state transformers (SST), E-STATCOM and other power-quality devices, medium-voltage switchgear, UPS, and liquid-cooling systems — is either new to the market, new to the supplier, or being built at a volume the supplier has never shipped before.

The NPI Engineer owns the path from "the supplier has a design" to "the equipment is qualified, manufacturable at rate, and running reliably on site." You sit between our electrical and mechanical design teams, our supply chain and quality teams, and the supplier's engineering and factory organizations, and you make sure every new product or major variant clears the gates — EVT, DVT, PVT, FAT, SAT — before it is trusted with production load. This is a hands-on role: you will spend real time on supplier factory floors, in test labs, and at site commissioning.

What you'll do

  • Own the NPI program for each new power or cooling product (BESS, inverters, SST, E-STATCOM, MV switchgear, UPS, CDUs, chillers) from concept selection through ramp, including the gate schedule, exit criteria, and risk register.

  • Drive early supplier design engagement: translate our site requirements (fault current, grid interconnection, harmonic and ride-through requirements, thermal envelopes, footprint, serviceability) into product requirements and specifications the supplier can build to, and negotiate trade-offs with their engineering teams.

  • Lead DFM/DFT/DFx reviews with suppliers so designs are manufacturable at the rate we need, testable in the factory, and serviceable in the field.

  • Plan and run prototype and pilot builds: define EVT/DVT/PVT scope and sample counts, witness builds, own test plans (type testing, HALT/HASS, thermal, EMC, protection coordination, functional and integration tests), and drive root cause and corrective action on every failure.

  • Qualify the product for deployment: define and execute first-article inspection, factory acceptance testing (FAT), site acceptance testing (SAT), and integrated system testing with the rest of the electrical and cooling chain, and sign off on production readiness.</

About the Role

We're looking for a software engineer, reliability-minded but still a builder, to own what happens in production to the Kubernetes-native control plane that provisions and runs our GPU inference fleet. The platform team builds the manifest-driven API and controllers that let the inference team declare what they need, a cluster, a model deployment, a capacity change, and get it reconciled underneath. Your job is to keep that promise true in the real world: triaging InfiniBand issues when prefill and decode nodes stall exchanging KV cache over RDMA, diagnosing hero-model and LoRA-serving faults that don't show up in generic health checks, and extending the automated self-healing system so each new failure mode becomes a permanent fix instead of a recurring page.

The core value we're after is keeping the decoupling real even when things break, and keeping the fleet efficient without that efficiency becoming a new source of instability. You'll own SLOs and error budgets for inference serving, lead incident response, and turn what postmortems teach you into actual changes in the controllers and automation, not just updated runbooks. You'll also work the reliability side of capacity efficiency, since a mistuned defragmentation or bin-packing pass is itself a production risk. Strong candidates have hands-on production-reliability experience on large-scale distributed or GPU-serving systems, are comfortable troubleshooting InfiniBand/RDMA and Kubernetes controller/CRD-based platforms, and think about GPU infrastructure, and the tools that keep it reliable, as software to be engineered.

A product mindset applies: the on-call experience, the clarity of an alert, and the judgment built into an automated remediation are things you ship and iterate on.

Responsibilities

  • Operate the provisioning state machine in production: own the health of the host lifecycle pipeline, discovery, inference bring-up, GPU driver/CUDA validation, health checks, decommission/RMA, triaging stuck or failed state transitions at fleet scale and feeding real failure patterns back into how the states and transitions are designed.
  • Triage and extend automated self-healing: when the node-scanning and remediation platform misses something, a new failure mode, an InfiniBand issue in disaggregated prefill/decode serving, a GPU Xid variant, a hero-model or LoRA-specific fault, diagnose it live, drive the fix to production, and turn it into a new detection/remediation plugin so it's automatic the next time.
  • Own end-to-end reliability of the pipeline: hold the SLOs and error budgets for provisioning and fleet health, lead incident response when idempotency, retry, rollback, or drift assumptions break down in practice, and drive the systemic fix, not just the hotfix.

About the Role

We're looking for a software engineer to build the Kubernetes-native control plane that provisions and runs our GPU inference fleet. You'll design a manifest-driven API where the inference team declares what they need, whether that's a cluster, a model deployment, or a capacity change, and our controllers handle the reconciliation, provider/runtime selection, and lifecycle management underneath, so the inference team never has to know or care which specific serving stack, scheduler, or hardware pool is doing the work. You'll also build the systems that keep the fleet efficient, not just running, including defragmentation and rebalancing logic that consolidates scattered workloads back into contiguous capacity, and scheduling/bin-packing improvements that push GPU utilization up without hurting latency.

The core value we're after is decoupling the people building on top of the platform from the operational and runtime complexity underneath, while squeezing more usable capacity out of the same hardware. You'll build the controllers, reconciliation loops, and self-service surface (API/CLI, not tickets) that make that decoupling real, plus the event-driven health, remediation, and utilization systems that keep it running and efficient without a human in the loop. Strong candidates have hands-on experience with Kubernetes controller/CRD patterns, have built or operated a platform API that abstracts multiple backends behind one interface, understand GPU scheduling and capacity efficiency (fragmentation, bin-packing, right-sizing), and think about GPU infrastructure as software to be engineered.

You will spend most of your time on active sites, acting as our team's eyes, voice and technical judgment in the field. You don't need a data center background. We care more about whether you have delivered complex industrial projects from the field and can get contractors and partners to act when you have no formal authority over them.

What you'll do

Be our engineering presence on site. You will walk installed work against the approved design and build working relationships with developers, general contractors, engineers of record, vendors and commissioning teams. You will settle what you can on the spot and bring in the right discipline engineer for the rest. Clear the path to commissioning and handover. You will check the interfaces between power, cooling, controls and structure before they surface as test failures. You will drive RFIs, deviations and field changes to decisions, so that open engineering questions don't hold up the crews.

Bring the field back into the design. You will turn recurring site problems into changes to our design

About Us

Twitch is the world’s biggest live streaming service, with global communities built around gaming, entertainment, music, sports, cooking, and more. It is where thousands of communities come together for whatever, every day.

The Twitch UX Monetization team is responsible for helping streamers monetize on Twitch through viewer engagement across our product experiences. A Senior UX Designer on the Monetization Team is expected to lead design work at the program level, work with senior XFN partners, represent work to executive leadership, guide and mentor junior designers and will report directly to the Monetization Director of Design.

  • Combine qualitative and quantitative information to develop hypotheses about customer motivations and use that to improve your designs
  • Present your work to others by participating in design reviews and feedback sessions
  • Mentor and grow junior designers and help instill best practice

jobs.title: Data Center Power Generation and Microgrids Engineer
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Training and serving frontier AI models requires compute infrastructure at a scale and density that pushes past what conventional data center designs were built to handle. The loads involved are large enough — and arrive fast enough — that utility supply alone often can't meet the need on the timeline required, and the step-load behavior of large accelerator clusters creates power-quality and ride-through demands that conventional backup-generation designs weren't built for. Anthropic's Data Center Infrastructure team is responsible for solving that problem: delivering facilities that can be energized early, ride through grid disturbances, and present a well-behaved load at the point of interconnection (POI).

As a Data Center Power Generation & Microgrids Engineer, you'll own the behind-the-meter generation and storage architecture for Anthropic's data center portfolio. That means the on-site generation fleet — reciprocating engine gensets, gas turbines, fuel cells — and the battery energy storage systems that buffer load steps and provide ride-through. It means the microgrid layer that ties them together: islanding and resynchronization, black-start, load-shedding, and generation dispatch. And it means the grid side: interconnection studies and agreements, IEEE 1547/2800 compliance, and power quality at the point of interconnection. You'll also own our temporary- and bridging-generation strategies — the plans that let a site energize and start serving load before permanent utility service is available, and transition cleanly once it is.

This is a deeply cross-functional role. You'll work closely with colleagues across the infrastructure team on where and how generation and storage tie into the site electrical distribution, controls, and SCADA, and with our hardware and compute teams to understand the load characteristics you're designing against. You'll be Anthropic's technical counterpart to on-site generation providers, BESS integrators, utilities, and ISOs/RTOs. Expect roughly 20–35% travel for design reviews, factory witness testing, and site startup.

Responsibilities

On-site generation engineering

  • Own Anthropic's behind-the-meter generation architecture across the portfolio — prime-mover selection and sizing (reciprocating engines, gas turbines, fuel cells), paralleling topology, redundancy, fuel systems, and emissions controls — and maintain the generation basis of design and technical specifications that build partners and generation providers design again

jobs.title: People Operations Partner

jobs.title: Senior Project Manager
jobs.description:
Senior Project Manager

Scopely is seeking a highly motivated Senior Project Manager to join our Playgami team on-site in Barcelona!

At Scopely, we care deeply about what we do and want to inspire play every day - whether in our work environments alongside our talented colleagues or through our deep connections with our communities of players. We are a global team of game lovers who are developing, publishing, and innovating the mobile games industry, connecting millions of people worldwide daily.

Playgami is building the best SaaS gaming platform ever! The team strives to create the world’s best products for game production, operation, and insights. Powering many award-winning, loved-by-millions franchise games over mobile, web, and PC.

As a Senior Project Manager, you will be collaborating with multiple development teams to build new features and platform integrations for our portfolio of games.

Your main responsibility is to ensure those teams operate in a framework that enables them to visibly, consistently and predictably deliver top of the market features, servicing millions of players. You will be operating close to our Games as part of our Solutions team and support Engineering in building custom solutions using our technology to fit our games’ needs.

What We’re Looking For

  • Must have 5+ years of experience as a project manager or producer
  • Demonstrated success managing multiple major and concurrent projects
  • A master of communication at all levels within a team or organization
  • You are a strong influence

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager (Roadmap) - Star Trek Fleet Command
jobs.description:

As the Senior Product Manager, you will be the product owner for key monetisation and engagement initiatives across the live game. jobs.title: Sr. Manager, QA Engineering & Automation
jobs.location: US - Culver City, California, United States; US - United States
jobs.description:
Scopely is looking for a Senior QA Manager, Automation & Tooling to join our team supporting a soon-to-be-announced AAA mobile game title. This role can be remote in the US and Canada, or hybrid in Culver City.

You will lead the automation strategy for a live game, building the people, processes, frameworks, and tooling required to scale quality across frequent releases and a large, active player base. You will partner closely with Engineering, QA, Live Operations, and other disciplines to establish a development culture where automation is a shared responsibility and a core component of product quality.

At Scopely, we create and operate games played by millions of people around the world. This role is an opportunity to shape how quality engineering evolves from the ground up for a high-scale live mobile game.

What You Will Do

  • Build and lead an automation team from the ground up, including hiring, team structure, processes, mentorship, and career development.
  • Design, build, and implement automated testing across UI, API, integration, regression, end-to-end, mobile, and live-operations workflows.

  • Provide hands-on technical leadership through framework design, prototypes, code reviews, automation implementation, and test-script development.
  • Mentor manual testers as they develop coding and automation skills, while defining metrics for coverage, stability, flakiness, execution time, and defect detection.
  • Communicate quality risks, automation progress, and investment needs while partnering with Product, Live Operations, Marketing, Customer Support, Localization, and external development teams.
  • Champion quality and release excellence across the organization while ensuring automation supports—not replaces—strong exploratory and risk-based testing.

What We’re Looking For

  • 8+ years of experience in QA, test automation, or quality engineering, including 4+ years leading or building automation teams.
  • Proven experience creating automation strategies, frameworks, tooling, and infrastructure for complex products, ideally from the ground up.
  • Experience evaluating automation app

jobs.description:
Scopely is looking for a Director, Slate Operations to join our Slate Development Group team in the UK remotely or in Barcelona, on a flexible hybrid model.

At Scopely, we care deeply about what we do and want to inspire play every day - whether in our work environments alongside our talented colleagues or through our deep connections with our communities of players. We are a global team of game lovers who are developing, publishing and innovating the mobile games industry, connecting millions of people around the world daily.

Slate Operations keeps Scopely's game development slate moving.   • Be the operational point of contact for specific in-development games — running the GDF cadence and connecting game and central teams so decisions get made once and aren't re-litigated. The main goal is to be the end to end steward for game teams in the game development framework.
  • Deliver operational excellence within our internal team, shaping our service model, priorities, and ways of working. Evolve our capabilities as needs change.
  • Drive the cross-slate operating model so independent game teams reuse what already works instead of rebuilding it.
  • Bring structure to consequential decisions — organize the inputs, assumptions, and trade-offs early so the owners and the room can reach real alignment before committing.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Data Infrastructure
jobs.description:
Summary

Scopely Explore (formerly known as Niantic) seeks a Software Engineer to design and build the data infrastructure and experimentation platforms that power our mobile games. You will develop systems that help game, product, analytics, and engineering teams run trustworthy experiments, understand player behavior, and make better decisions at scale.

This is a hands-on technical leadership role. You will write production code, make foundational architectural decisions, and operate critical distributed systems while guiding the technical direction of the platform. Beyond individual technical contribution, you will help lead and grow the Data Infrastructure organization by aligning engineers and cross-functional partners, mentoring engineers, and driving multi-team initiatives from strategy through delivery. Depending on team structure and business needs, this role may also include formal people-management responsibilities. We seek creative engineers with excellent technical judgment, strong interpersonal skills, and an eagerness to embrace new technologies and AI-native development methodologies. Do you want to build the foundations that enable faster learning and better player experiences across Scopely Explore?

Responsibilities

  • You design, build, and operate scalable data infrastructure and experimentation systems for both general product experimentation and game-specific use cases.
  • You lead the technical design of capabilities such as experiment assignment, player segmentation, exposure logging, telemetry processing, metric computation, guardrails, and reproducible analysis.
  • You build reliable batch and streaming data pipelines using technologies such as Apache Beam, Apache Spark, Ray, Apache Flink, and Apache Kafka.
  • You design data platforms on GCP using technologies such as BigQuery, Apache Iceberg, Google Cloud Storage, Kubernetes, Airflow, and Terraform.
  • You remain hands-on throughout the development lifecycle, contributing production code and solving complex problems in distributed computing, streaming, orchestration, and storage.
  • You develop effective methodologies and guardrails for AI-assisted and agentic engineering, including context management, automated validation, evaluations, human review, and responsible adoption.
  • You use AI-native workflows across your end-to-end responsibilities, including architecture exploration, implementation, testing, code review, documentation, debugging, incident response, and platform operations.
  • You maintain ownership of the correctness, security, performance, and maintainability of all work produced with AI assistance.
  • You evaluate new technologies pragmatically and apply them where they materially improve engineering velocity, platform reliability, or experimentation quality.
  • You lead the technical direction and delivery of the Data Infra

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer (Backend) - WWE Champions
jobs.description:
Scopely is looking for a Senior Software Engineer (Gaming Backend) to join our WWE Champions team in the United States or Canada on a remote basis or Mexico City on a hybrid basis.

What We’re Looking For

Experience & Technical Skills

  • 6+ years of professional software development experience in gaming or large-scale live-service applications
  • Deep expertise in backend engineering with high-level server-side languages and frameworks
  • Experience collaborating with game client engineers (e.g., Unity/C#)

jobs.title: Senior UX Designer - Monster Hunter Now
jobs.description:
The UX Design team of Scopely Explore (formerly known as Niantic) delivers innovative mobile experiences that inspire exploration, exercise, and connection for players around the world.

As a Senior UX Designer, you will own the end-to-end UX vision for a game title or major feature area, carrying it from strategy and underlying flows through polished, high-fidelity interfaces that keep the player at the center. The design challenges here are real-world and often have no established playbook, so we value thoughtful design, exceptional visual execution, and the ability to bring ideas to life quickly.

At Scopely Explore and our Tokyo Studio, great UX depends on how you collaborate as much as what you produce. You will operate as a peer to Product, Engineering, Art, and Marketing to influence product direction, and one of your most important and rewarding partnerships will be with Game Designers, who bring deep expertise in shaping player experiences. Together, you will work at the intersection of deep game design and the accessibility of a great consumer product, building experiences that welcome gamers and non-gamers alike.

Within the design team, you will raise the craft of the designers around you through mentorship, and part of that is helping define how we work with AI. You will help shape best practices and experiment with AI tools and workflows to form a point of view on where they add real value. Your efforts will underscore core UX and design principles, showing that the best results come when the designer and user-centric thinking stay at the center, so that AI amplifies product impact rather than substituting for creativity.

What you will do

  • Own the end-to-end UX vision and strategy for a game title or major feature area, from concept through implementation.
  • Define interaction patterns, design approaches, and the quality bar for player-facing experiences, navigating undefined problem spaces with minimal direction.
  • Produce high-fidelity UI, mockups, wireframes, prototypes, and design documentation: polished visual work that communicates clearly and validates direction early.
  • Drive cross-functional alignment and influence product direction in close partnership with Game Design, Product, Engineering, Art, and Marketing.
  • Facilitate ideation and feature planning by framing the problems worth solving, not only responding to them.
  • Explore and apply AI tools and workflows where they strengthen the work, with a clear point of view on when to use them and when not to.
  • Elevate the design practice: mentor designers, give and gather critique, share workflows and emerging tools, and help level up the team.
  • Advocate UX decisions persuasively to internal and external stakeholders, building shared understanding and buy-in.
  • Regular and reliable attendance and participation in meetings; in-office Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thur

jobs.title: Sr.Client Security Engineer
jobs.description:
Location: Tokyo, Japan(On-board in China)

Scopely's Security team is looking for a Sr Client Security Engineer to build a new client security function in China. You will design and ship client/server-side protections for large-scale mobile games, combat sophisticated cheating ecosystems, and help ensure fair play for tens of millions of players.

What You Will Do

  • Build, and grow the Client Security team in China, setting China specific technical direction, and operational best practices.
  • Design, implement, and maintain client-side detections against third‑party cheating tools, modified clients, hooking frameworks, and emulators on Android and iOS.
  • Own the client security integration into Scopely's internal anti-cheat platforms working closely with teams to ensure detections are actionable and scalable.
  • Define and evolve the obfuscation and hardening strategy for China mobile builds (e.g., binary protection, anti-debugging, anti-tamper, integrity checks), including evaluating and integrating third‑party hardening vendors where appropriate.
  • Build and maintain strong coverage for the China mobile ecosystem, including:
    • distribution through multiple Android app stores and OEM devices,
    • diverse OS/ROM variants and rooted/jailbroken environments,
    • and local PC/emulator-based cheating patterns.
  • Contribute hands-on code (C++ plus Java/Kotlin and/or Objective‑C/Swift) in security‑sensitive paths, including detection logic, integrity checks, and secure client–server protocols.

What You Will Need

  • Experience in mobile security, game anti-cheat, or client-side security engineering, including time working directly on Android or iOS native code.
  • Direct experience with reverse engineering.
  • Deep hands-on experience with:
    • Android and IOS internals
    • hooking and instrumentation frameworks,
    • and common mobile client security attack vectors.
  • Strong proficiency in C/C++ and at least one mobile native language (Java/Kotlin for Android or Objective‑C/Swift for iOS), including experience shipping production code in large apps.
  • Demonstrated experience designing and shipping client-side anti-cheat or integrity systems that integrate with server-side enforcement or analytics pipelines.
  • Prior experience ing or technically directing a small engineering team
  • Experience working with large-scale telemetry or anti-abuse pipelines and using data to tune detections and reduce false positives.
  • Professional proficiency in both Mandarin and English, written and spoken
  • Requires five days per week in the office
  • Requires relocation to Tokyo

jobs.title: Senior Cloud Data Platform Engineer
jobs.description:
Senior Data Platform Engineer

Scopely is looking for a Senior Data Platform Engineer to join our Playgami Data Platform team.

At Scopely, we care deeply about what we do and want to inspire play every day - whether in our work environments alongside our talented colleagues or through our deep connections with our communities of players. We are a global team of game lovers who are developing, publishing, and innovating the mobile games industry, connecting millions of people worldwide daily.

Playgami builds technology for game teams across Scopely. Our Data Platform provides the shared foundation that enables teams to use data safely and reliably at scale, supporting 15+ games and 2,000+ active users across Scopely and processing more than 60TB of data per day.

What You’ll Do

As a Senior Data Platform Engineer, you will build and improve the shared infrastructure, tooling, and services that power data and analytics teams across Scopely.

You will investigate platform needs, evaluate technical tradeoffs, and turn agreed priorities into tested code and reusable infrastructure. Working closely with data and analytics teams, Security, and Governance, you will take platform improvements from technical design through deployment and operation.

Your main responsibility will be to improve the security, reliability, scalability, and efficiency of our Data Platform while making it easier for teams to build and operate their data workloads.

You will lead the technical design and delivery of platform improvements, making informed tradeoffs between reliability, security, scalability, and cost as part of a shared team roadmap.

  • Build and operate shared GCP and BigQuery infrastructure using Terraform, automated checks, and CI/CD.
  • Build scalable, self-service platform capabilities that enable data teams to develop, deploy, and operate workloads with less manual support.
  • Improve user and service account access, ensuring least-privilege principles and dependable approval, review, and revocation processes.
  • Translate Security and Governance requirements into practical controls for sensitive data and data sharing.
  • Improve Airflow and Cloud Composer reliability through troubleshooting, staged upgrades, and tested recovery processes.
  • Improve cloud data platform performance and cost efficiency using workload and capacity insights.
  • Build actionable monitoring and alerts, investigate incidents, and implement improvements to prevent recurring failures.
  • Partner with teams to understand their needs, investigate platform challenges, evaluate potential solutions, and help shape the technical roadmap.
  • Make platform workflows easier to adopt and operate through documentation, runbooks, and mentoring.

크래프톤 AI Research 본부는 사내외 여러 분야와 협업 하여 다양한 문제에 대한 AI 솔루션을 제공하며, 자체 딥러닝 기술 연구를 통해 우리만의 서비스를 개발합니다. 그 방향성은 크게 두가지입니다.
  • 딥러닝 기술 개발을 통한 게임 제작 효율성 및 보편성 증대
  • 유저와 함께 게임 플레이를 할 수 있는 Co-Playable Character (CPC) 개발
[AI Research]
AI Research 팀의 연구는 대규모 언어모델(LLM)의 작동 원리를 깊이 이해하는 데서 출발합니다. 이를 바탕으로 게임 제작 효율화와 새로운 플레이 경험을 가능하게 하는 핵심 기술을 만들어 갑니다. 박사후 연구원이 LLM 연구에 깊이 집중할 수 있는 환경을 갖추고 있습니다.
  • LLM의 표현력·추론·일반화 메커니즘을 이론적·경험적으로 분석하며, 효율성·안정성·성능을 끌어올릴 수 있는 새로운 관점과 알고리즘을 모색합니다.
  • Language Model 기반 Agent 기술을 발전시켜 게임 환경을 스스로 이해하고 유저와 자연스럽게 상호작용하는 Gaming Agent를 구현합니다.
  • 게임을 넘어 Physical AI 영역까지 연구 범위를 확장하며, 인터랙티브 인텔리전스의 다음 단계를 그려나갑니다.
  • Scaling laws, reasoning, tool calling, agentic RL, efficient training, multi-modal grounding, omni-model, world models 등 LLM의 핵심 주제들을 폭넓게 다루고 있습니다.
[Culture Fit]
AI Research 본부 인원들은 다양한 프로젝트를 통하여 여러 분야의 팀원들과 교류하고 협업하며 다양한 문제에 창의적인 아이디어를 제시할 수 있습니다. 나이 및 직급에 관계없이 자유롭게 의견을 개진하는 분위기가 장려됩니다.
다양한 문화적 배경을 가진 인원들이 모여 팀을 이루고 있으며 활발한 소통을 위해 통·번역 등 언어적 장벽을 해소할 수 있는 방법들을 적극 지원하고 있습니다.
AI Research 본부는 연구자가 깊이 있는 탐구에 집중할 수 있는 환경을 지향합니다. 대규모 LLM 학습·실험을 수행할 수 있는 연구 인프라를 갖추고 있으며, 학회 참여·발표 등 외부 연구 활동을 적극 지원합니다. 연구자들이 서로의 전문성을 나누며 함께 성장할 수 있는 환경을 제공합니다.

우리 팀과 함께할 미션을 소개합니다.

크래프톤 AX(AI Transformation)는 전사에 AI를 도입하여, 데이터와 인프라를 기반으로 임직원들의 워크(Work)와 워크플로우(Workflow) 자동화를 가속화하고 그 압도적인 효율화 성과를 전사로 확산하는 핵심 조직입니다.
Data Foundation 팀은 파편화된 전사 데이터를 통합하고, AI(LLM, AI Agent 등)가 즉각적으로 이해하고 활용할 수 있는 최적의 데이터 구조(Ontology)와 아키텍처를 설계·구축합니다.
크래프톤의 각 조직이 실제로 사용하는 데이터와 업무 맥락을 깊이 이해하고, 이를 AI가 이해할 수 있는 데이터 관리·활용 체계로 직접 기획하고 설계해 낼 분을 모십니다.

우리 팀과 함께할 미션을 소개합니다.

담당 도메인의 데이터 관리·활용 체계를 직접 기획·설계하고, 설계 산출물(Ontology 설계서, 데이터 모델, 거버넌스 기준 문서 등)을 주도적으로 작성·관리합니다.

  • 도메인별 데이터 구조 분석 및 Ontology 설계: 도메인의 원천 데이터와 업무 프로세스를 분석하고, AI(LLM, AI Agent)가 활용할 수 있는 Ontology(개체·관계·속성 정의) 구조를 주도적으로 설계하며 Ontology 설계서를 작성·관리
  • 비즈니스 용어·지표 정의 및 데이터 거버넌스 기준 수립: 도메인별 핵심 용어(Glossary), 지표 정의, 데이터 오너십·접근 권한 기준을 현업과 협의해 수립하고 거버넌스 기준 문서로 정립
  • 데이터 품질·정합성 분석 및 개선: 원천 데이터의 정합성, 완결성, 중복 여부를 분석하고, 개선 방안을 직접 도출해 Ontology 설계 및 데이터 구축에 반영
  • 현업 부서와의 요구사항 분석 및 데이터 모델링: 담당 조직의 실무자를 인터뷰하고 업무 데이터를 분석하여, 실제 질의·분석 시나리오에 맞는 데이터 모델(테이블 구조, 관계, 계층)을 설계·구축하고 지속적으로 개선

  • SQL을 능숙하게 다루며, 원천 데이터를 스스로 탐색·분석해 구조를 파악할 수 있는 분
  • 특정 업무 도메인의 데이터와 프로세스를 깊이 이해하고, 현업과 커뮤니케이션하며 요구사항을 구조화해 데이터 모델·지표 체계로 설계해 온 경험이 있는 분
  • 데이터 모델링(테이블 설계, 정규화, 관계 정의 등)을 직접 기획·수행해 본 경험이 있으신 분

With bold imagination and breakthrough technology, we create unforgettable worlds for fans across the globe.

Art Department 소개

Art Department는 크래프톤 게임 스튜디오의 아트 프로덕션 전반에 필요한 그래픽 기술과 솔루션을 지원하는 조직입니다. 그래픽 기술과 제작 파이프라인을 기반으로, 게임 개발팀이 빠르고 안정적으로 프로젝트를 시작하고 확장할 수 있도록 지원하며, 크래프톤만의 차별화된 아트 기술 서비스를 제공합니다
Art Dept는 “Scale-up the Creative”와 “AI-first”라는 회사 방향성 아래, 장인정신에 기반한 높은 퀄리티, 데이터 기반 최적화, 그리고 제작 효율화를 핵심 가치로 삼고 있습니다.
조직 구성원은 Advanced 그래픽 기술과 최신 트렌드를 선도하며, 전사 스튜디오를 대상으로 최적화된 제작 가이드라인을 제시하는 기술 파트너로서 역할을 수행합니다. 단순한 툴 지원을 넘어, 제작 과정에서 발생하는 기술적 병목을 선제적으로 해결하고, 스튜디오와의 협업(Co-development)을 통해 최상의 개발 경험을 제공합니다.
Art Department는 경험과 신뢰를 바탕으로 국내외 다양한 스튜디오를 지원하며, 지속적으로 성과를 만들어가고 있습니다. 크래프톤 게임이 높은 그래픽 완성도를 갖추고 성공적으로 시장에 출시될 수 있도록, 함께 성장할 전문가를 기다립니다.

Visual R&D 팀을 소개합니다.

Visual R&D 팀은 KRAFTON Art Department 산하 조직으로, 예술적 창의성(Art)과 기술적 구현(Technology)의 시너지를 극대화하는 역할을 수행합니다.
우리는 게임 개발 과정에서 마주하는 다양한 난제를 해결하고, 크래프톤 산하 글로벌 스튜디오들이 최고의 퀄리티를 효율적으로 구현할 수 있도록 최적화된 솔루션과 제작 환경을 제공합니다.
현재 우리는 인게임 캐릭터 제작의 혁신을 목표로 하는 'VCC(Visual R&D Character Customization)' 프로젝트를 비롯하여, 차세대 그래픽 기술 연구와 개발 프로세스 고도화 업무를 주도하고 있습니다.
우리의 목표는 단순한 R&D를 넘어, 실제 프로젝트에 즉시 적용되어 성과를 낼 수 있는 실용적인 기준을 만드는 것입니다.
우리는 지금, 변화하는 개발 환경 속에서 유연한 사고와 협업을 통해 새로운 가치를 창출하고 프로젝트의 완성도를 높여갈 인재를 찾고 있습니다.
각 분야의 전문성을 바탕으로 크래프톤 전사 프로젝트의 성공을 함께 지원하고 성장하고 싶은 분들의 도전을 기다립니다.

  • IT 서비스 프로세스 개선 및 인프라 최적화

jobs.title: [KRAFTON JUNGLE] 정글 과정 마케팅 실행 및 운영 지원 (3~5년 / 계약직)
jobs.description:
우리는 게이머의 로망을 실현하기 위해, 누구도 가지 않는 길을 갑니다.

우리 팀(프로젝트)을 소개합니다.

  • 크래프톤은 2022년부터 사회 공헌 사업의 일환으로 ‘크래프톤 정글’을 출범하여 기술 산업의 미래 인재, SW 개발자를 양성해오고 있습니다.
  • 크래프톤 정글은 경기도 용인에 위치한 크래프톤 정글 캠퍼스에서, 자기 주도적 학습과 몰입 경험, 팀 기반의 프로젝트 수행을 바탕으로 기본기가 탄탄한 개발자로 성장하게 하는 교육 과정을 운영하고 있습니다.
  • Jungle Operations & Outreach Team은 정글의 사업을 관리하며, 정글 브랜드 관리, 교육생 모집을 위한 마케팅 캠페인 실행, 지원 및 선발 절차, 교육 과정의 주요 행사, 교육생 지원과 같은 크래프톤 정글의 전반적인 사업과 운영을 담당합니다.
  • 정글의 지속 성장을 위하여 더 효과적인 마케팅 운영안을 설계/실행하고, 팀과 협업하여 정글을 성장시키는 여정에 참여하고 싶은 분을 기다립니다.

우리 팀과 함께할 미션을 소개합니다.

Jungle Operations & Outreach Team은 동료를 존중하는 태도와 끈기 있고 성숙한 사고, 긍정적인 에너지를 바탕으로 팀의 방향성에 맞추어 적극적으로 협력하는 팀 플레이어를 찾고 있습니다.

  • [주요 역할]
    • 정글 교육 과정의 성과 극대화를 위하여 효과적인 캠페인 전략을 기획/실행하며, 타 사례와 정글의 캠페인 결과를 분석하고, 더 효과적인 실행 방안을 도출합니다.
    • 캠페인 정성/정량 데이터를 수집하고, 데이터 기반의 성과 분석 프로세스 및 대시보드 구축을 실행합니다.
    • 교육생 모집 선발, 학사운영 및 입소식, 수료식, 발표회 등 주요 교육 행사와 프로그램의 준비 및 실행, 운영을 지원합니다.
    • 교육과정이 원활하게 운영될 수 있도록 기타 운영 업무 전반을 지원합니다.
  • 이 직무를 통해 이런 경험을 할 수 있습니다.
    • 교육 사업 기반의 캠페인 설계 및 실행, 교육 사업 분야에 대한 전문적 인사이트와 업무 경력을 축적할 수 있습니다.
    • 교육 사업의 브랜드 관리와 마케팅 실행, 사업 및 학사 운영을 아우르는 통합적인 브랜드 육성 경험을 쌓을 수 있습니다.

이런 경험을 가진 분과 함께 성장하고 싶습니다! (필수요건)

  • 기업(교육, 서비스, IT 계열) 또는 전문 에이전시에서 통합 마케팅 기획/실행의 PM 수행 경력
  • 능동적으로 솔루션을 제시할 수 있는 적극적인 마인드와 긍정적인 에너지
  • 맡은 업무를 꼼꼼하게 확인하고 책임감 있게 마무리할 수 있는 분
  • 다양한 사람들과 원활하게 커뮤니케이션할 수 있는 분
  • 해외 출장에 결격 사유가 없는 분

이런 경험들이 있다면 저희가 찾는 그 분입니

jobs.title: [Palworld Mobile] System Designer (3년 이상)
jobs.description:
우리는 게이머의 로망을 실현하기 위해, 누구도 가지 않는 길을 갑니다.
예상을 뛰어넘는 과감한 상상력과 기술로, 전 세계 팬들이 잊지 못할 세상을 만들기 위해 담대하게 도전하고 개척합니다.

We pioneer the path to players' dreams.
With bold imagination and breakthrough technology, we create unforgettable worlds for fans across the globe.

우리 팀(프로젝트)을 소개합니다.

  • Palworld Mobile은 원작의 오픈월드 경험을 유지하면서도, 언제 어디서나 빠르게 몰입할 수 있는 게임 플레이를 제공하고자 합니다.
  • 모바일에 최적화된 인터페이스와 터치 기반 조작 시스템을 통해 손안에서 펼쳐지는 무한한 모험의 세계를 즐길 수 있도록 설계하려 합니다.
  • 원작의 방대한 오픈월드와 생존, 제작 시스템, 다양한 Pal과 함께하는 즐거움을 유지하면서도, 모바일 환경에 최적화된 플레이로 만들어 나갈 예정입니다.
  • Palworld Mobile에서만 경험할 수 있는 새로운 기능과 콘텐츠로 진일보된 게임 플레이 경험을 선사하고자 합니다.

우리 팀과 함께할 미션을 소개합니다.

  • 커뮤니티 등의 아웃 게임 시스템 디자인
  • 이벤트 시스템
  • 로그인, CDN, 운영툴 연동 등의 서비스 및 운영에 필요한 기능 기획
  • 업적, 퀘스트, 성장 등 기본 시스템 구현 및 개선 작업

이런 경험을 가진 분과 함께 성장하고 싶습니다! (필수요건)

  • 최소 3년의 관련 게임 기획 경력
  • 원작 팰월드 플레이 경험이 50 시간 이상인 분
  • 기획 의도를 컨셉화하고 능동적으로 제안하며, 이미지/툴/데이터테이블 등으로 시스템 구조를 구체화하는 능력
  • 다양한 구성원들과 피드백을 주고받으며, 성장을 추구하시는 분
  • 모바일 플랫폼을 고려하여 UI/UX 기획이 가능하신 분
  • 해외 출장에 결격 사유가 없는 분

이런 경험들이 있다면 저희가 찾는 그 분입니다! (우대요건)

  • 팰월드 뿐만 아니라 러스트, 언던(모바일) 등의 생존 게임을 100 시간 이상 플레이한 경험
  • 이벤트 및 결제 시스템에 대한 업무 경험

크래프톤의 도전에 함께 하기 위해 아래의 전형 과정이 필요합니다.

  • 서류 전형 > 사전 인터뷰 (Phone Interview) > *과제 전형 > 인성검사 (Personality Assessment) > 직무면접 (Technical Fit Interview) > 종합면접 (2-3회) (Culture Fit Interview) > 합격 및 입사
  • *해당 절차는 각 포지션 및 후보자에 따라 변동이 있을 수 있습니다.
  • 상시 채용으로 채용 완료 시 조기 마감될 수 있습니다.
  • 필요 시, 인터뷰 및 직무 테스트가 추가될 수 있습니다.

jobs.title: [PUBG Franchise] Art Director (10년 이상)
jobs.description:
우리는 게이머의 로망을 실현하기 위해, 누구도 가지 않는 길을 갑니다.
예상을 뛰어넘는 과감한 상상력과 기술로, 전 세계 팬들이 잊지 못할 세상을 만들기 위해 담대하게 도전하고 개척합니다.

We pioneer the path to players' dreams.
With bold imagination and breakthrough technology, we create unforgettable worlds for fans across the globe.

우리 팀(프로젝트)을 소개합니다.

  • PUBG IP를 기반으로 신작 및 transmedia 확장 프로젝트의 비주얼 방향성을 수립하고, IP 전반의 visual foundation을 체계화하며, 내부 및 외부 제작을 전략적으로 리딩하는 조직입니다.
  • 단순 제작 조직이 아니라, IP Visual Core 및 세계관 고도화 / Franchise 확장을 위한 장기적 visual system 구축 / 외부 파트너 및 스튜디오 협업 관리 / 병렬 프로젝트 대응 및 QC 체계 확립을 담당하는 전략 실행 조직입니다.

우리 팀과 함께할 미션을 소개합니다.

PUBG IP Universe의 core visual foundation 및 세계관 고도화를 리딩하며, 동시에 외부 제작 및 병렬 프로젝트 대응을 매니징합니다. 비주얼 기준을 정의하고 문서화하며, 내외부 제작 파트너가 동일한 방향성과 품질 기준으로 실행할 수 있도록 alignment와 QC 체계를 구축하고 운영합니다. 본 포지션은 최종 Art Director의 방향성과 승인 하에 운영되며, IP 기준 생산과 외부 실행 운영 기능을 분담하여 프로젝트 속도와 일관성을 강화합니다.

  • PUBG IP Universe의 core visual boundaries 정의 및 Visual Foundation 고도화

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Frontier AI is on track to be among the most consequential and most adversarially-targeted technology in the world. The capability curve is steep, the adversaries who want these systems are extremely well-resourced, and the security bar this will eventually require is well beyond where the industry operates today. Incremental hardening alone is not going to close that gap, so we need breakthroughs and a group of people to go find them.

Security Labs is that team. We run a portfolio of high-risk, high-expected-value security projects: the work that seems impractical until someone optimistic and stubborn enough actually tries it. Projects run on the order of weeks rather than quarters, and each one is either handed off to the Anthropic team that will own it in production or wound down with a writeup of what we learned. We expect a meaningful fraction of our bets not to land.

This team is intentionally scrappy and ambitious. We're intentionally iterating fast on high-risk research bets and we expect a meaningful fraction not to land. If a 30% project success rate sounds uncomfortable, or uncharted and chaotic territory isn’t both frightening and exciting, this probably isn't the right fit. There are other places in Anthropic Security doing important work with more structure, less risk, and more certain paths to positive outcomes.

The questions we're trying to answer include:

  • Can our core research workflows survive extreme isolation?
  • Can we replace trust with cryptographic guarantees?
  • Can the models themselves become our most effective security control?
  • What would it actually take to defend against a tier-1 state adversary, and how much of that can we build now?

Who we're looking for. We're hiring generalists with rare depth. You're a strong software engineer as a baseline, and on top of that you've gone deep in at least one area most engineers don't get near: firmware or hardware security, applied cryptography, OS / kernel / hypervisor internals, formal methods, reverse engineering, or high-assurance and cross-domain systems. You've built things under your own direction, you're comfortable jumping layers when the problem demands it, and you'd rather take a swing at something that might not work than ship the safe incremental thing. Every dollar Anthropic earns and every dollar it spends on compute has to reach the books correctly, and the volume grows with Claude usage. You will shape its architecture. Its users include Claude agents, which read and write through the same APIs and controls as people.

  • Drive the build of the accounting ledger and engine: an append-only ledger with idempotent posting, a rules framework that turns business events into journal entries, translation into the ERP, and period locks
  • Design and build the SDKs and frameworks that finance apps and agents build on
  • Build controls into the platform as code: immutable audit trail, maker-checker, scoped access and segregation of duties

  • Shape the platform’s technical direction: architecture, engineering standards and design reviews

About Anthropic

If you're excited about interpretability research and open to an individual contributor role, we encourage you to apply.

About the Interpretability team

When you see what modern language models are capable of, do you wonder, "How do these things work? How can we trust them?"

The Interpretability team’s mission is to reverse engineer how trained models work, and Interpretability research is one of Anthropic’s core research bets on AI safety. We believe that a mechanistic understanding is the most robust way to make advanced systems safe.

People mean many different things by "interpretability". We're focused on mechanistic interpretability, which aims to discover how neural network parameters map to meaningful algorithms. Some useful analogies might be to think of us as trying to do "biology" or "neuroscience" of neural networks, or as treating neural networks as binary computer programs we're trying to "reverse engineer".

We aim to create a solid scientific foundation for mechanistically understanding neural networks and making them safe (see our vision post). We have focused on resolving the issue of "superposition" (see Toy Models of Superposition, Superposition, Memorization, and Double Descent, and our May 2023 update), which causes the computational units of the models, like neurons and attention heads, to be individually uninterpretable, and on finding ways to decompose models into more interpretable components. jobs.title: Staff+ Software Engineer, VectorDB
jobs.location: New York City, NY | Seattle, WA; San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic is looking for a Staff+ Software Engineer to work on the vector search infrastructure behind Claude. Retrieval is how Claude learns about the world. Web search across claude.ai, the API and agentic surfaces, memory across conversations, and the reinforcement learning workloads that train our next models all depend on fast, cheap, high-recall nearest-neighbor search over billions of vectors.

You'll join a small team responsible for the vector database layer that serves Claude's retrieval workloads: its architecture, performance, scalability and cost. This is a foundational role. The team is small, core architectural decisions are still open, and the engineers who join now will shape how the system evolves.

The role sits in our Databases organization and works day to day with the Search Platform team, which owns web search indexing, retrieval and serving, and the Memory & Search team, which owns search and memory inside claude.ai.

We're looking for someone who has built vector or search systems that ran in production, at scale, with real users and a real on-call. You'll be hands-on in the code, and you'll also be the person deciding how the pieces fit together.

Key responsibilities

  • Own the core of Anthropic's vector database layer: index structures, storage layout, query execution and the serving layer
  • Own production readiness - benchmarking against exact search, capacity planning, onboarding new workloads, and the operational tooling to run it at scale
  • Drive the recall, latency and cost trade-offs - quantization, filtered search, index build and refresh strategy, and how compute and storage are separated and scaled
  • Scale throughput by an order of magnitude as research and training demand grows, and work out whether the bottleneck is architecture, hardware or engineering bandwidth
  • Extend the retrieval stack toward hybrid retrieval - lexical search and fused ranking alongside vector search
  • Set the evaluation methodology for the system - recall targets, latency objectives, cost per query, and the regression detection that keeps them honest
  • Set technical direction for a growing team - lead design reviews, make architectural decisions others build on, and mentor the engineers joining the effort
  • Share the on-call for the systems you own

Minimum qualifications

  • Direct experience building a vector database or approximate nearest-neighbor search system that ran in production at scale

jobs.location: San Francisco, CA | Seattle, WA | New York City, NY | Washington, DC
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the team

Anthropic's Security Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) team is the connective tissue that holds the company accountable to its security commitments. We translate regulatory, customer, and voluntary obligations into controls that teams act on, and give leadership a bird's-eye view of how well we're meeting them. We're building toward a fundamentally different kind of GRC: one that directs Claude, with the right humans in the loop, to challenge and evidence the performance of controls continuously rather than through periodic audits.

Within Security GRC, Audit & Assurance runs the integrated audit across our frameworks and maintains the Common Control Framework the program hangs off. This role sits in Audit & Assurance and helps run that integrated audit program, plan the audits we add next, and assess the frameworks and scope changes we are considering.

About the role

You'll help run Anthropic's unified audit program: quarterly audits across SOC 2, HIPAA and the ISO 27000 family including ISO 42001, plus the rest of our certifications, working with our audit firms, our GRC Partners, and control owners across the company. You'll plan new audits as we expand to new frameworks, platforms and regions, and run the gap assessments that tell us what each expansion takes before we commit to it.

You'll help build the audit operating model and runbook, and drive automation in the program so evidence is collected once and reused across frameworks, requests reach control owners once, and each audit cycle takes less effort than the last. Building with Claude is a normal part of the job, with you deciding where human judgment stays in the loop.

This is an individual contributor role for someone with program management experience who writes clearly, stays calm under deadlines, and likes making a busy program simpler.

Key responsibilities

  • Run the audit program as a program: one integrated plan and calendar across audits and expansions, with milestones, dependencies, risks and decisions tracked, and regular status to GRC leadership and stakeholders
  • Plan and run the quarterly audits, from scoping through report and findings closeout
  • Run audit readiness ahead of each fieldwork window: control owner prep, evidence pre-checks and walkthrough dry runs
  • Scope each audit's boundary with Product and Engineering: which products and deployment paths are in scope, and flag when a launch or new platform chan

jobs.title: Product Designer, Safeguards
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Design at Anthropic sits at the intersection of craft, research, and product intuition. We're a small team working on products that millions of people use daily—and on interactions that don't have established conventions yet.

Our work shapes how people experience AI: whether Claude feels like a tool or a collaborator, whether it earns trust or erodes it. We partner closely with engineers and researchers, often designing around capabilities that are emerging in real-time. That means staying close to the models, prototyping rapidly, and being comfortable with ambiguity.

We're looking for designers who ship fast and stay in motion—people who would rather get something in front of users this week than perfect it for a month. You're excited to question fundamental UI assumptions and invent patterns that feel native to AI, and you're already using tools like Claude Code to extend what you can build. You pay attention to where model capabilities are heading, not just what Claude can do today, and you find ways to keep caring about the pixels, the copy, and the edge cases while shipping quickly.

Key responsibilities

  • Collaborate with product managers, engineers, AI researchers and other stakeholders to define product vision, strategy and roadmaps, and play an active role in shipping.
  • Understand the technical architecture of our products and define primitives for new capabilities.
  • Define feature areas with exceptional attention to detail and polish, identifying opportunities to improve quality and consistency of broader flows
  • Craft beautiful, polished, and delightful user interfaces that build trust and showcase the power of our AI technology
  • Comfortable in code, design, prototypes, and learning new ways to communicate ideas and concepts
  • Find creative ways to ship high-quality work in a fast-paced, often ambiguous, resource-constrained startup environment

Minimum qualifications

  • Experience designing and shipping complex workflows, enterprise/B2B SaaS, developer tools, or API products end-to-end
  • Proven track record of executing end-to-end on large and complex products, or a series of products, in ambiguous environments
  • A portfolio demonstrating user-centered design thinking and polished UI craftsmanship
  • Proficiency with modern design and prototyping tools, such as Figma
  • Experience using AI tools such as Claude Code as a creative partner in you

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Internal Comms
jobs.description:
About Us

Twitch is the world’s biggest live streaming service, with global communities built around gaming, entertainment, music, sports, cooking, and more. It is where thousands of communities come together for whatever, every day.

We’re about community, inside and out. You’ll find coworkers who are eager to team up, collaborate, and smash (or elegantly solve) problems together. We’re on a quest to empower live communities, so if this sounds good to you, see what we’re up to on LinkedIn and X, and discover the projects we’re solving on our Blog. Be sure to explore our Interviewing Guide to learn how to ace our interview process.

About the Team

The Twitch community is like no other - a passionate and engaged group of creators and active participants who are uniquely invested in what we’re all building together. The Marketing & Communications team at Twitch serves to authentically activate the Twitch community (and beyond) in ways that inform and inspire. Members of our team work across a range of areas including internal and external communications, content & partnerships, creative services, and marketing strategy.

About the Role

We’re looking for someone to lead internal communications across the company. You’ll help employees understand what’s happening and why it matters, help navigate complex company moments and transitions, and develop company All Hands programming that people look forward to.

It’s a role with range. One day you might be shaping comms for an organizational change; the next, developing a new All Hands segment or finding a great story buried somewhere in the company. We’re looking for someone with excellent judgment, strong instincts, and real creative ambition — someone who runs toward the hard stuff and is always thinking about how to make internal communications more useful, interesting, and engaging. Keeping employees informed and connected, and finding ways to highlight and celebrate our people, our work, and our community, are at the heart of this position.

You can work in New York, NY; San Francisco, CA; Los Angeles, CA; Irvine, CA; or Seattle,WA.

You Will:

Manage Internal Comms

About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Every time Claude runs code, uses a computer, or works as an agent, it does so inside a sandbox. Our Sandboxing team builds the isolation layer behind that work. The same systems run the code Claude writes for users, the environments we train and evaluate models in, and the agents our customers deploy.

These workloads are untrusted by design, and there are a lot of them. Sandboxes need to start in milliseconds, hold up under adversarial code, and scale to a very large number of concurrent sessions. You will work at the boundary between the Linux kernel, virtualization, and the container ecosystem. You will partner with research, product, and security teams to make sure that safe and fast do not trade off against each other.

Key responsibilities

  • Design, build, and operate the sandboxing infrastructure that runs untrusted, model-generated code and agent workloads at scale

  • Improve sandbox startup time, density, and throughput, including snapshot and restore, checkpointing, and warm pools

  • Strengthen isolation across compute, filesystem, and network, including egress controls and per-session credential handling

  • Investigate and fix performance, reliability, and security issues at the kernel, hypervisor, and container runtime level

  • Build the monitoring, tracing, and debugging tools that show where time and resources go inside a sandbox

  • Work with researchers to support reinforcement learning environments and evaluations that need fast, reproducible, isolated execution

  • Work with product and platform engineers to expose sandboxes as a dependable, well-designed capability for Claude products and customers

  • Partner with security teams to threat-model the platform and to test, harden, and respond to escape and abuse scenarios

  • Work with cloud providers on the hardware and platform features that our workloads depend on

  • Share knowledge on systems programming and Linux internals, and help set technical standards for the team

  • Strong programming skills in at least one systems language such as Rust, C, C++, or Go

  • Working knowledge of virtualization or container isolation technologies such as KVM, QEMU, Firecracker, gVisor, or runc

jobs.title: Tabletop Exercise Lead, The Anthropic Institute
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About The Anthropic Institute

The Anthropic Institute (TAI) is a function within Anthropic that works to advance the public conversation around AI.

The Institute is comprised of research teams tackling some of AI's most consequential societal challenges: the Frontier Red Team, which stress tests our systems against catastrophic risks; Societal Impacts, which studies how Claude is used by millions of people; Economic Research, which tracks AI's impact on people's jobs and the larger economy; the Rule of Law team, which studies AI's impacts to democracy; and more.

The Institute's mission is to reduce information asymmetries between Anthropic and the outside world, name and answer the hard questions implied by powerful AI systems, and publish these findings so that policymakers, researchers, technology leaders, and the public can reckon with what's here and what's to come.

About the role

The role. You will build and lead the Institute’s tabletop exercise program and the team that runs it. Based on trends visible in the exponential and in consultation with technical experts, you will set the research agenda: which questions the exercises should answer, which scenarios to run, with which audiences, and what each run is meant to test. You will own the methods that make results comparable across runs and turn them into findings people outside the room can use. You will hire and manage a team plus a bench of facilitators, and you will be the program’s public voice.

Why tabletop exercises? If RSI arrives, the hardest problems will be about making decisions under uncertainty. The people making them may not trust each other, and the authorities they work under may not be fit-for-purpose. A tabletop exercise (TTX) allows the people who would face that situation practice it before it is real. It also shows us what tools and information they reach for, including what they would need that does not exist yet.

Tabletop exercises are also a research method. You can run the same scenario many times, with different groups of people (and with many more AI agents playing in silico), and you start to see the distribution of decisions people make. This is one of the few ways to generate empirical evidence about the future, i.e., how people and institutions will respond to situations that have not happened yet.

Key responsibilities

  • Set the program’s research agenda: the questions exercises should answer, the scenarios to run, and the audience for each

About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. About the role

Reinforcement learning is how Claude learns to reason, write code, and act autonomously over long horizons. At frontier scale, an RL run is an unusually demanding distributed system. Training, sampling, and environment execution run concurrently across a large fleet of accelerators and hosts, exchange data continuously, and have to keep making progress while hardware fails, load shifts, and the research changes underneath them. How well that system holds together determines how much of our compute turns into learning, and how quickly the team can try the next idea.

As a Research Engineer on the Distributed Systems team within RL Engineering, you'll work on whatever part of that system is the current limit. That might be scheduling and placement, data movement between components, running large numbers of sandboxed environments, storage and checkpointing, networking, fault tolerance, autoscaling, or the observability that tells us what a run is actually doing. We're looking for generalists: engineers who can move between these layers, reason from first principles about a system they haven't seen before, and pick the problem that matters most rather than the one closest to their prior experience.

Our system changes as fast as the research does, correctness under failure matters as much as throughput, and the best solutions often come from understanding the ML workload well enough to know which guarantees it actually needs. Strong candidates have built and run large distributed systems, care about getting the details right, and want to apply that experience to a workload that is very large, very heterogeneous, and changing quickly.

Key responsibilities

  • Design, build, and operate the distributed systems that run RL at scale, across training, sampling, and environment execution
  • Find and remove whatever currently limits the system, whether it's scheduling, data movement, storage, networking, or coordination
  • Build fault tolerance into every layer: failure detection, isolation, and recovery that keep long-running jobs making progress without human intervention
  • Design resource management and autoscaling so that compute follows demand as a run's needs shift
  • Build observability that makes it possible to understand what a run is doing and why it slowed down, stalled, or produced unexpected results
  • Build automation that detects and remediates common problems, and design interfaces that let engineers and automated tools operate runs safely

jobs.title: Research Engineer, Post-Training Model Evaluations
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic's production models undergo sophisticated post-training processes to enhance their capabilities, alignment, and safety. Decisions in production training depend on knowing how the model is really behaving. Our team's mission is to have the best observability into production post-training runs at Anthropic: to be the clearest, most trusted view of model quality during training. We shape what gets measured, keep the signal trustworthy and timely, and get to the bottom of surprising results to inform post-training and release decisions.

In this role you will lead the science of how we evaluate production training runs. You'll work out which measurements tell us something real about the model, notice when they stop doing so, and find what we should be measuring but aren't. You'll partner with research teams across every RL domain, bringing their priorities into what we measure and setting the standard for what makes an eval trustworthy across post-training. You'll also be hands-on with the eval fleet day to day, because the best questions about measurement come from watching real results come in during a live run.

Responsibilities

  • Steer the eval strategy for production Claude models: study and optimize the eval mix so it gives the most accurate and complete assessment of model quality
  • Run and monitor the eval fleet live to understand how each Claude model is developing as it trains
  • Advise teams across post-training on eval methodology, and help eval authors bring new evals up to the bar for production
  • Investigate regressions in production runs and inform training interventions when appropriate
  • Build the dashboards, alerts, and reports that researchers and leadership use to track model quality

You may be a good fit if you

  • Have designed, run, and analyzed evaluations for ML models at scale
  • Care deeply about measurement quality, thinking twice before trusting a number
  • Can turn ambiguous results into clear recommendations, and are comfortable influencing direction across teams
  • Have strong Python skills and are comfortable working with production systems
  • Maintain clarity and rigor when debugging complex, time-sensitive issues
  • Thrive in controlled chaos and are energized, rather than overwhelmed, when juggling multiple urgent priorities during a live training run
  • Care about the societal impacts of your work and about shipping frontier mo

jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

As Claude reaches more people, including individuals, businesses, developers building on our APIs, and the platforms and resellers building on top of those, knowing who is on the other side of a request and what they are allowed to do becomes foundational to running our products responsibly. Creating a centralized identity, verification, and access system that every Claude surface draws on is important to accomplishing our mission.

We are hiring a Product Manager to own the safe access. The primitives are the building blocks the rest of Anthropic uses to manage access to models and capabilities: access programs, accounts, organization linking, verifications, user APIs for platforms, and the internal tooling teams use. You will own the end-to-end product experience and strategy for internal and external access,, across every surface.

This is a role for a strong executor with the ability to be agile in shipping in a 0-1 product space. Safe access is a new product that sits on the critical path of every model launch and every access program. Requirements arrive from many organizations at once, and most weeks you will be the person defining the problem rather than receiving it.

Key responsibilities

  • Own the product strategy and roadmap for the account and access primitives, with the goal that any team at Anthropic can provision access or run an access program with minimal support. This is highly ambiguous and requires a lot of cross team coordination and deep understanding of the systems of today.
  • Own the end-to-end experience of getting and managing access for internal stakeholders (research, model launches, safeguards, go-to-market) and for external customers and partners, and keep it consistent across every surface. This requires thinking through many user types, with vastly different experiences.
  • Support the API designs and the UX of the access APIs that platforms, resellers, and internal services integrate with. Work through the designs with engineering and make calls on the primitives yourself.
  • Partner with the trusted access and verification product managers so that new programs compose from shared primitives rather than one-off builds.
  • Coordinate across the product, safeguards, legal, and go-to-market teams, and drive alignment when their requirements conflict.

Minimum qualifications

  • Are a strong executor with a track record of shipping through ambiguity and cross-organization dependencies.
  • Write clearly enough

  • Lead investigations into emerging fraud patterns, building multi-layered defenses designed for attacker adaptation rather than point-in-time rules
  • Work cross-functionally with finance, support, legal, and data science, and with external payment processors and platform partners

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Proficiency in Python, SQL, and data analysis tools
  • Experience building or operating fraud, risk, or abuse detection systems in production
  • Strong communication skills and ability to explain complex technical tradeoffs to non-technical stakeholders

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 8+ years of industry software engineering experience, with a focus on payments fraud or risk
  • Fluency with payments rails: card network

About the role

Governments do some of the most consequential work there is: deciding benefits claims, getting veterans to care, investigating financial misconduct, running unemployment insurance, and producing the analysis that world leaders act on. Anthropic's public sector team exists to put Claude in the production path of that work. In the US and some allied governments, Claude is already in daily use across major agencies and US states.

The next steps need a particular kind of product manager: someone who can walk into an institution they have never worked with, sit with the people doing the work and find, alongside them, the workflow that matters. The best government products we know of started as an idea that came out of the room rather than a requirements document.

The scope is large: a product portfolio here is a set of governments rather than a feature area. A year in, success looks like agencies delivering services more effectively because public servants are doing core parts of their job with Claude in the loop, and at least one thing that you learn from them shipping to every Anthropic enterprise. That is a lot of surface; you will have to choose where to go deep, and we will back the choice.

We are hiring across civilian, state and local, govtech, and national security portfolios and will match you to one on background and interest. Some portfolios require eligibility for a US security clearance, though most do not. You would be among the first product managers on the team, working with a dedicated engineering and research team and with the policy, go-to-market, customer success, and applied AI leads who already spend their days inside these agencies.

This role sits in the Planning pillar, on the Demand Planning team, and works daily with research engineering, pretraining, inference, compute supply, finance, and external vendors.

You own the tranches. The job has two halves that feed each other. Upstream, you take the Demand Planning forecast and turn it into per-tranche requirements — shape, interconnect, region, supporting resources, date — and carry those into sourcing negotiations and data center build reviews so we contract for capacity we can actually use when we need it. Downstream, you own the integrated schedule and system of record for every tranche in flight — from contracted through reserved, ingested, in-cluster, healthy, and occupied — and you drive the owners of each hop to their dates. Every slip you see downstream becomes a contract-language fix, an automation, or a correction fed back to the forecast.

What you'll do

  • Turn the forecast into per-tranche requirements. Take the Demand Planning forecast plus direct input from research, pretraining, and inference planners, and convert it into concrete accelerator, interconnect, region, supporting-resource, and date requirements for each tranche. Represent those in sourcing negotiations and data center build reviews, including which contractual terms actually move delivery dates.
  • Qualify tranches for deliverability before signature. The Capacity Planner signs fit-to-forecast; you sign whether the shape can land schedulable, healthy, and instrumented in that region on that date, with storage, egress, identity in place.
  • Close the delivery loop. Track forecast-versus-delivered on shape, region, and timing for every tranche; publish the variance; and feed it back to Demand Planning and into the next contract.
  • Own the bring-up system of record. Define the canonical contract-to-occupied state machine with explicit entry and exit criteria per stage, and make it a first-class object in the capacity data layer

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. About the Role

Anthropic's inference fleet serves Claude to millions of users across our own products and the world's largest cloud platforms. The stack that makes this possible is deep and tightly coupled: accelerator kernels, model servers, distributed routing, autoscaling, capacity management. Every layer affects the others, often in ways that are hard to see in isolation.

The Inference System Dynamics team is responsible for understanding that whole system and holding it to a high bar across four dimensions: throughput, latency, reliability, and correctness. We measure how the fleet performs against its theoretical performance frontier, run cross-layer investigations to explain the gaps, and own the correctness checks that make sure Claude's outputs are right, not just fast, across hardware platforms and serving configurations. We don't own the individual components. We instrument and model them, find the highest-leverage opportunities across them, and partner with the owning teams to land the wins.

You'll work across all four areas. One week that might mean tracing a tail-latency regression from request timing down through routing and batching into a kernel overhead; the next it might mean tightening a correctness eval so it catches an output regression introduced by a quantization change. We're looking for performance engineers who treat correctness as part of performance.

Key Responsibilities

  • Run cross-layer performance investigations across throughput, latency, and reliability, sizing the gap between actual fleet performance and theoretical rooflines, identifying root causes, and quantifying the value of closing them

  • Build the observability, dashboards, and modeling tools that make throughput, latency, cost, reliability, correctness, and their interactions legible across the stack
  • Partner with kernel, serving, routing, autoscaling, and capacity teams to prioritize and land the highest-impact optimizations your analysis surfaces
  • Ruthlessly stack-rank a large surface area of opportunities by impact and effort, and say no to the ones that don't make the cut

About the role:

Anthropic's Application Security team secures the systems that build, serve, and increasingly are Claude. The attack surface is unlike most AppSec work: multi-agent orchestration, sandboxed code execution, agents holding delegated credentials, untrusted tool output crossing trust boundaries — problems with little prior art and no off-the-shelf playbook.

The way the team works is also different. We use Claude as our primary tool across every part of the job: it drives our static analysis, drafts and fixes vulnerabilities as pull requests, performs first-line bug bounty triage, and assists threat modeling for design reviews. The human work is the judgment layer — system-level reasoning, deciding what matters, and building the next thing the model can't do yet.

This is a builder's role on a senior team. We hire engineers who ship production systems and clear a hands-on threat-modeling bar — people who can find the vulnerability but would rather build the system that finds them all. Every engineer owns a system end-to-end, and the team's work has shaped customer-facing product security — including Claude Code's security review tooling, its security guidance plugin, sandboxing, and auto mode.

Key responsibilities:

  • Design, build, and operate Claude-powered security systems — LLM-driven code analysis, automated vulnerability remediation, AI-assisted threat modeling — and own one or more of them end-to-end, including the cross-functional relationships that come with it
